item.title: A problem with the containment procedures
item.content:encoded: As far as I can tell, there isn't any reason for the necklace to be on a mannequin at all times, so couldn't a "drowning in snake blood" Scenario be avoided just by keeping the necklace close enough to the floor of the case that the blood is never far enough away not to be drawn back into the necklace? It just seems like common sense.

item.title: regarding the comments
item.content:encoded:
First, thanks for the suggestions and comments.

Tabbyclaw, The Major and FullHazard: with the addition of the new containment requirements and the second addendum, are you still interested in wearing it or cutting it in half?

To the others, I'm not sure yet what I should do about the fact that the test subjects reaction to 533 was more or less understandable and natural. I'm leaning towards letting that part stand.

item.content:encoded: See, I really like the fact that it seems to be completely endless. The fact that it makes the wearer uncomfortable is cool, I suppose, but the endless snake crawling through some sort of metal filling is fuckawesome and upvoteable. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Very well imagined and well-written, but I agree it could use a bit more to up the creep factor.

I like the constriction angle laranos suggests- maybe instead of making people feel uncomfortable (which seems like a natural reaction to a headless, endless living snake thing), wearers instead have a strong compulsion to keep it ON, even as it begins to slowly tighten around them? Maybe that's too straightforward, but I'll leave that to you to figure out. Not bad for your first effort :]
